title: Partcraft solver test: solver-neutral case catalogue
units: millimetres and radians; right-handed, y up; arcs run counter-clockwise from start to end

cases.title: Horizontal constraint on a line
Vertical constraint on a line
Horizontal constraint between two points (no line)
Vertical constraint between two points (no line)
Two points coincident
Point on a (fixed) line
Point on a circle (centre fixed, radius dimension 10)
Point on the circle of an arc (centre fixed, radius dimension 10)
cases.notes: planegcs treats point-on-arc as point-on-circle (GCS.cpp:1009); the angular span is not enforced.

cases.title: Point on an open cubic B-spline (poles fixed)
cases.notes: planegcs needs the curve parameter u as an extra unknown (point_on_bspline); u0 is only the starting value for it.

cases.title: Line tangent to a circle (centre fixed, radius 5, line start fixed)
Line tangent to the circle of an arc (centre fixed, radius 5)
Two circles tangent from outside (radii 5 and 3)
cases.notes: planegcs decides external/internal when the constraint is created, from the current centre distance (GCS.cpp:1111).

cases.title: Small circle tangent inside a big circle (radii 10 and 3)
Two counter-clockwise arcs meeting tangentially at an end point (radii 5 and 3, the small one curls inside the big one)
cases.notes: Endpoint tangency = coincident + tangent direction (angle via point). Internal tangency, so both ccw arcs continue without a cusp.

cases.title: Line ending tangentially on an arc (radius 5)
Two lines of equal length
Two circles of equal radius (first has radius dimension 5)
Circle and arc of equal radius (circle has radius dimension 4)
Two arcs of equal radius (first has radius dimension 5)
Two lines parallel (first line fixed)
Two free lines parallel
Two lines perpendicular (first line fixed)
Two free lines perpendicular
Fix a point at given coordinates
Fix, unfix, fix again at another place
cases.notes: Unfix = removing the constraint: the point must stay where it is and gain its 2 DOF back.

cases.title: Fix both end points of a line
Point at the midpoint of a fixed line
Line end follows the midpoint: P1 and M fixed, so P2 = 2M - P1
Point at the middle of an arc (composed: on the circle and on the bisector of the chord)
cases.notes: Arc midpoint has no planegcs constraint; composition: point-on-arc + point-on-perpendicular-bisector(S,E).

cases.title: Arc concentric with a circle (circle radius 5)
Two circles concentric (radii 5 and 8)
Second line collinear with a fixed first line
Two points symmetric about a fixed vertical axis
Two points symmetric about a fixed centre point
Point mirrored about the fixed diagonal y = x
G2 join of two arcs (composed: coincident + tangent + equal radius)
cases.notes: Two arcs with equal signed curvature and a common tangent at the joint lie on the same circle: expect centre of A2 = centre of A1 and radius 5.

cases.title: G2 join of an arc and an open cubic B-spline at the spline start
cases.notes: planegcs has no curvature constraint (no match for "urvature" in planegcs/ and Sketch.cpp). Needs a new constraint class, impossible in the prebuilt WASM.

cases.title: Distance between two points = 10
Distance of a point from a fixed line = 4
Horizontal distance P1 -> P2 = 12
Vertical distance P1 -> P2 = -7 (P2 below P1, signed convention y2 - y1)
Length of a line = 10
Angle from L1 (fixed, horizontal) to L2 = 30 degrees
Direction angle of a line (to the x axis) = 120 degrees
Radius of a circle = 7
Radius of an arc = 6
Diameter of a circle = 14
Diameter of an arc = 12
Arc of radius 5 with length 5*pi/2 (quarter circle)
Reference distance P1-P2 (geometry set by driving distance_x/y = 6/8)
Reference distance of a point from a line
Reference horizontal distance
Reference vertical distance
Reference line length
Reference angle between two lines
Reference radius of a circle through a fixed point
Reference diameter of a circle through a fixed point (README of the package lists this type as faulty)
Reference arc length (README of the package lists this type as faulty)
Reference radius of an arc
Reference length on a free line: nothing moves, DOF stays 4
A free line has 4 degrees of freedom
Rectangle constrained step by step to 0 DOF, then a redundant and a contradicting dimension
cases.notes: Steps: free (8) -> horizontals (6) -> verticals (4) -> width (3) -> height (2) -> fix corner (0) -> redundant top length (0, redundant) -> contradicting top length (conflict).

cases.title: Two length dimensions of one line (10 and 20)
Horizontal + vertical + length 10 on one line (contradiction)
Horizontal + vertical on one free line (no contradiction, the line collapses to a point)
cases.notes: Mathematically consistent (dx = 0 and dy = 0). A CAD would have to refuse this; we only record what the solver does.

cases.title: Triangle with sides 3, 4 and 10 (violates the triangle inequality)
cases.notes: No structural dependency at the start: diagnosis by Jacobian rank (GCS.cpp:4738) cannot name the conflict, so the conflict check is soft.

cases.title: Both lines horizontal AND parallel: one of the three constraints is redundant (consistent)
The same horizontal distance dimensioned twice (consistent duplicate)
Symmetry (2 equations) plus midpoint (2 equations) share one equation: partially redundant
cases.notes: symmetric(A,B about the vertical axis) = {A.y = B.y, A.x + B.x = 0}; midpoint(M of AB, M = (0,5)) = {x sum = 0, y sum = 10}. One equation is shared, the other of each tag is not.

cases.title: Open cubic Bezier: its first pole coincident with the end of a line
cases.notes: Pole 1 is the curve start (clamped knots), so a point-point coincident is enough.

cases.title: Open cubic Bezier: line ends tangentially at the spline start (G1)
cases.notes: FreeCAD refuses slope constraints at end knots (Sketch.cpp:3091); the end tangent is the direction of the first control leg (Geo.cpp:713).

cases.title: Periodic (closed) cubic B-spline, 6 poles; distance between pole 1 and pole 4 = 12
cases.notes: Periodic knots 0..6, multiplicity 1 each, 6 poles (OCCT convention used by planegcs).

cases.title: Point on a periodic cubic B-spline (poles fixed)
Degree 2 spline with interior knots: a line touches it tangentially at knot index 2
cases.notes: Interior knot multiplicity 1 < degree 2, so the slope is defined there (ConstraintSlopeAtBSplineKnot, Constraints.cpp:262).

cases.title: Cubic spline, interior knot multiplicity 2 (C1): a line touches it tangentially at that knot
cases.notes: Knots 0,1,2 with multiplicities 4,2,4: sum 10 = 6 poles + degree 3 + 1.

cases.title: Cubic spline with an interior knot of multiplicity 3 (C0 kink at pole 4): a line tangent at the kink
cases.notes: The slope at a kink is not defined: FreeCAD refuses it (Sketch.cpp:3081-3103) and ConstraintSlopeAtBSplineKnot asserts numpoles >= 2. A track may answer "no"; if it answers "yes" the checker tests both one-sided slopes.

cases.title: Rational quadratic B-spline = exact quarter circle of radius 5; a free point on it must end up at distance 5 from the origin
cases.notes: Tests weights: the poles carry weights 1, sqrt(2)/2, 1.

cases.title: Isosceles triangle, one side stepped 10 -> 100 in 10 steps, each solve starts from the previous result
cases.notes: The apex P3 must stay above the base (no mirror flip) and move continuously.

cases.title: Line of length 40 rotated in 15 degree steps from 10 to 355 degrees (passes +-pi)
cases.notes: Angles are compared modulo 2*pi; the free end must move along the circle without jumping.

cases.title: Circle tangent to a line, radius stepped 10 -> 50 (centre x fixed at 0); it must stay on the same side of the line
Drag the free end of a line of fixed length 10 around, mouse always at distance 14 (end must follow along the circle of radius 10)
cases.notes: Drag = temporary constraints (tag -1 / temporary:true) on the point; they must not make the system fail and are not kept.

cases.title: Chain of 10 links (length 5), origin fixed; the tip is dragged in small steps along an outward spiral inside the reach: it must reach the mouse position
cases.notes: Dragging a point with abundant DOF: expected tip = mouse within 1e-3. The chain starts slightly curved and a little off in length.

cases.title: Connected chain of 6 fully dimensioned rectangles (48 elements)
Connected 5x5 grid of fully dimensioned rectangles (200 elements)
Connected 5x25 grid of fully dimensioned rectangles (1000 elements)
Chain of 40 links (length 5), origin fixed; 100 drag steps of the tip along an outward spiral (timing of a drag sequence)
cases.notes: Positions stay inside the reach (200).
